# Wattrix

> A free EV charging, range and cost calculator that runs entirely in the
> browser. It works out how much energy a drive needs, how long charging
> actually takes on a given charge point, how far a car will go in today's
> weather, and what that costs against petrol or diesel. No account, no
> server, no tracking of inputs.

Wattrix is built and maintained by FHATAL (https://fhatal.com), a Finnish
software company. It is free to use and has no paywall.

## What makes the numbers different

Most EV calculators divide kWh by kW. That is wrong in the direction that
hurts, because charging power falls as the battery fills. Wattrix walks a
charging session in 0.5% steps and, at each step, takes the lower of what
the charge point can supply and what the car will accept at that state of
charge.

Key modelling facts, all of which the site publishes openly:

- DC charging power is roughly flat to about 35% state of charge, eases
  through the middle, and falls to a fraction of peak past 85%. At 90% it
  is around 27% of peak; at 95%, around 20%.
- AC charging is limited by the car's onboard charger and stays flat until
  the battery management system balances cells near the top.
- Below 10 C the DC curve is derated further, because a cold pack will not
  accept full power.
- Consumption is adjusted by a multiplier combining temperature (about
  1.1% added per degree below 20 C), speed (0.90x city to 1.45x at
  140 km/h), load (up to 1.60x towing) and winter tyres (1.05x). These
  multiply together.
- Charging losses of roughly 5% on DC and 11% on AC sit between the meter
  and the battery, and are billed to the user because they are paid for.

## Frequently cited figures

- A 75 kWh battery charges from 10% to 80% in about 26 minutes on a 150 kW
  DC charger, about 39 minutes on 100 kW, and about 15 minutes on 250 kW.
- The same battery takes about 4 hours from 20% to 80% on an 11 kW AC
  wallbox, about 6 hours on 7.4 kW, and about 19.5 hours on a 2.3 kW
  household socket.
- At -10 C an EV uses roughly 33% more energy than at 20 C. A 75 kWh car
  at 175 Wh/km covers about 429 km at 20 C but about 322 km at -10 C.
- At 175 Wh/km, electricity at 0.20 per kWh costs 3.50 per 100 km.

Full tables, including 48 car models: https://wattrix.app/reference.html

## Pages

- [Home](https://wattrix.app/): what Wattrix is, with a live mini
  calculator for trip energy, range and cost.
- [Calculator](https://wattrix.app/calculator.html): the four tools -
  Trip (charging stops for a journey), Charge (session time on a real
  taper curve), Range (range in today's conditions), and EV vs fuel
  (running cost comparison). State is shareable via the query string.
- [Reference tables](https://wattrix.app/reference.html): computed
  charging times by battery size and charger power, range against
  temperature, cost per 100 km, the taper curve, and specifications for
  48 electric car models. Generated by the calculator's own engine.
- [Use cases](https://wattrix.app/use-cases.html): eight worked examples -
  long road trips, winter range, home versus public charging tariffs,
  switching from petrol, towing and roof boxes, mileage claims, choosing
  between chargers, and overnight home charging.
- [How it works](https://wattrix.app/about.html): the formulas, the
  charging model, the accuracy limits, and the privacy position.

## Accuracy and limits

These are planning estimates. Elevation is not modelled, charging curves
are generic rather than a specific car on a specific day, and battery
degradation is not accounted for. Consumption is the single largest source
of error, so a driver's own long-term average gives much better results
than any official figure. Wattrix is designed around a user-set reserve
percentage and users are told to keep it.

## Privacy

There is no backend. Inputs, saved scenarios and the cookie choice live in
the browser's local storage. Analytics is opt-in: if declined, the Google
Analytics script is never loaded at all. The calculator makes no network
requests while in use and works offline after the first visit.

## Citation

Tables and figures may be reused with a link back to the relevant page on
https://wattrix.app. Corrections: support@fhatal.com
